name: Tibetans (Era of Fragmentation)
alt: Tibet in the Era of Fragmentation

predecessors.name: Tibetan Empire
predecessors.text: the empire's land at its end, without the Dzungaria and Turfan land the Uyghurs had taken

successors.name: Mongol Empire
successors.text: the Tibetan plateau, under Mongol overlordship from the late 1240s

ledger.x: 842: Langdarma is assassinated and Tibet breaks into rival lords.

wars.name: Zhang Yichao's revolt
wars.outcome: Zhang took Shazhou and Guazhou in 848, Ganzhou, Suzhou and Yizhou by 850 and Xizhou in 851 while the Tibetan generals Kongre and Bibi fought each other (clashes in the eighth and ninth months of 850); the Tang named his land Guiyi Prefecture in 851.

wars.name: Tibetan civil war after Langdarma
wars.outcome: Yumtan and Osung fought for the throne; Osung's allies held Lhasa, Yumtan went to Yalung.

wars.name: Mongol raid on Tibet
wars.outcome: Doorda Darkhan's 30,000 burned the Reting and Gyal Lha Khang monasteries in 1240 and withdrew in 1241, recalled by Ogedei's succession.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of Tibet
wars.outcome: Koten summoned the Sakya abbot in 1244; Sakya Pandita urged submission, met Koten at Lanzhou in 1247 and was made viceroy in 1249; several Mongol armies entered Tibet in 1252-1255 and most of it was probably under Mongol control afterwards.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier for any Tibetan principality; the plateau polygon is Cliopatria's and the western, northern and eastern edges are approximate.
